subject: home-economics
timingNote: 2h 30m · 280 or 320 marks depending on the Section C option

tips.timing: About 30 minutes — answer any 10 of the 12 questions. Each question carries 6 marks, so keep each answer concise and move on after roughly 3 minutes.
tips.structure: Answer in the spaces provided on the paper. Match the number of distinct points to the marks available, use precise Home Economics terminology, and complete every requested table, label, calculation or example.
reminders: Read all 12 questions before settling on your best 10
Attempt extra questions only after completing the required 10
Give a separate, specific point for each available mark
Include units and show working in nutritional or financial calculations
Do not spend long-answer time developing a 6-mark response

tips.timing: About 85 minutes — Question 1 is compulsory and worth 80 marks; answer any two of Questions 2–5, worth 50 marks each. Budget roughly 38 minutes for Question 1 and 23–24 minutes for each chosen 50-mark question.
tips.structure: Follow the printed sub-parts in order and write in proportion to the marks. For discuss, assess or evaluate questions, make a clear point, explain it with course knowledge, and apply it to the named food, family, consumer or social context.
reminders: Choose the other two questions only after reading Questions 2–5
Use the supplied table, chart, image or case material explicitly when asked
Label every sub-part so the examiner can match answers to the paper
Support developed points with relevant examples from the course

sections.name: Section C – Elective or Core Option

tips.timing: About 35 minutes — answer one elective question or Question 4 (core), including part (a) and either part (b) or part (c). Electives 1 and 3 and the core option are worth 80 marks; Elective 2 is worth 40 marks.
tips.structure: State clearly which question and option you are answering. Develop part (a) fully, then answer only one of (b) or (c). Organise longer responses into focused paragraphs with a point, explanation and relevant Home Economics example.
reminders: Answer part (a) and either part (b) or part (c), not both
If you submitted Textiles, Fashion and Design coursework, you may attempt only Question 2 in this section
Check whether your chosen option is worth 40 or 80 marks
Keep enough time to complete every sub-part of the chosen question
Use subject-specific examples and terminology rather than generic statements
